client_brief:
Autumn shelf talkers that match the bottles and the sellable wine list

Cellar & Cru's autumn selection goes onto the shelf as a collection: every talker carries the Cellar & Cru key and vine mark, and every bottle should look as if it were photographed in the same light. We have sixteen photographs covering fourteen wines, taken on two evenings, and an old printer's PDF for the shelf talker.

Please prepare
- Wine shelf talker: 15 named exports. The bottle image matches the named wine. The vintage is accurate. The origin is readable. The price is easy to locate: the talker gives the wine's bottle price, and no other price.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street
brand_identity.sector: An independent fine wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers building by the glass lists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009, on a side street off the main shopping run in Edinburgh, Scotland. A small counter operation, one or two on the floor, an owner who buys the list himself.
brand_identity.about: Cellar & Cru is a merchant, not a shop that happens to sell wine. The owner tastes and chooses every line, and the selection changes with the season. When there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in, the shelf card is how a wine sells itself, so the card carries the grower, the region, the vintage, our note, the score and the price.
brand_identity.audience: Confident domestic drinkers and restaurant buyers aged 40 to 65 who read a shelf card the way a reader reads a review, and who treat visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent fine wine. Bottles from 14 pounds to 220. The card is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the line. Never the supermarket aisle, never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage.

palette.name: Cellar Ink
palette.usage: All type: the wine name, grower, region, vintage, style, buyer note and price, as talker_2025_PRINT.pdf sets them, and the wordmark. The key and vine device is this one solid ink, as it is printed in one ink on mark_card.jpg. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Claret
palette.usage: Only the short rule under the wine name, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never type, the price, a score, a ground or a panel.

palette.name: Vine
palette.usage: Optional. No supplied brand file gives it a role on the talker. If used, only as a small non-type accent, never type, the price, a score, a ground, a panel or any part of the key and vine device.

palette.name: Brass Key
palette.usage: Only the hairline under the wordmark, 0.2 mm thick and exactly 32 mm long, as the signature move sets it. Never type, a panel or a ring, and never a metallic or foil effect.

palette.name: Chalk White
palette.usage: The card ground throughout, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf, and the only ground or panel colour. Never type on the card.

palette.name: Stone Grey
palette.usage: Small labels, the score line, the picture keyline and the foot rule, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never the wine name, the buyer note, the price, a ground or a panel.

brand_identity.typography: Cellar & Cru runs two faces across four steps. Step 01 is the wine name in Eczar Regular 400 at 17 pt on 20 pt, tracking -0.01 em. Step 02 is the wordmark, CELLAR & CRU in Eczar Medium 500 caps at 7.5 pt on 10 pt tracked 0.30 em, fitted to a 32 mm measure above a Brass Key hairline 0.2 mm thick and 32 mm long, and set at 22 px on screen. Step 03 is the buyer's note, Eczar Regular 400 at 8.5 pt on 11.5 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line. Step 04 is the fine print, Akzidenz-Grotesk Next Regular at 7 pt on 10 pt in letterspaced small caps tracked 0.12 em for region, vintage and score, with the price in the same face at 9 pt tabular lining, plain in the run of the line. The hairline and its 32 mm measure never scale with the type.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, measured and honest, the owner describing a wine as if standing beside you. It says what a wine is and is not, without hyperbole. Example: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original mark artwork went with the designer who moved abroad. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us, carrying the mark at about 45mm. The autumn list, buyer's notes, scores and prices arrive from the till export.
brand_identity.values: A selection chosen by one buyer with a point of view, and a shop floor that sells wine honestly even when nobody is free to talk.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The wordmark is CELLAR & CRU in Eczar Medium caps tracked 0.30 em above a Brass Key hairline that is always exactly 32 mm long, never scaled with the type.

type_system.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street

scale.sample: Wine worth the walk down the side street
scale.note: The wine name. Flared cut serifs that read like a review. Existing size and leading kept exactly as the brand already sets them.

The wordmark, and the signature move. Point size is subordinate to the lockup: the line is always fitted to a 32 mm measure above a Brass Key hairline 0.2 mm thick and 32 mm long. Screen wordmark 22 px. The hairline never scales with the type.

scale.sample: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
scale.note: The buyer's note, set in the same face as the wine name directly beneath it. Maximum 65 characters a line. Existing size and leading kept.
Region, vintage and score. The price sets in the same face at 9 pt tabular lining, plain in the run of the line, never enlarged or emboldened.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is CELLAR & CRU in Eczar Medium 500 caps tracked 0.30 em, sitting above a Brass Key hairline that is always exactly 32 mm long and 0.2 mm thick. The lockup is fitted to that 32 mm measure at every size, so the point size follows the rule rather than the rule following the point size.
rules: The Brass Key hairline is always exactly 32 mm long and 0.2 mm thick, and never scales with the type.
The wordmark is always Eczar Medium 500 caps tracked 0.30 em, fitted to the 32 mm measure.
On screen the wordmark sets at 22 px.
The score is present but small, and the price stays plain in the run of the line: never colour, embolden or enlarge a price or a score.
Region, vintage, score and price are the only items in Akzidenz-Grotesk Next: 7 pt letterspaced small caps for words, 9 pt tabular lining for figures.
Never the supermarket aisle, and never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage: grower, region and vintage always lead the card.
Generous white space is part of the card, not a leftover.

palette_rules.distribution: Chalk White is the card ground and the only ground or panel colour, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. On it, all type is Cellar Ink, the price included, as talker_2025_PRINT.pdf sets its wine name, record values, note and price; small labels and the score line may be Stone Grey. The key and vine device is Cellar Ink, printed in one ink as on mark_card.jpg. Brass Key is only the hairline under the wordmark. Claret is only the short rule under the wine name. Vine, if used, is only a small non-type accent. Stone Grey, Claret and Vine together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, the key and vine device is never a ghosted or transparent watermark, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a bottle photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, rules, keylines, the key and vine device or panels. No price or score is set in Claret, Vine or Brass Key or reversed out of a ring, badge or panel: the type rules never colour, embolden or enlarge a price or a score. No metallic, foil or gradient effect on any colour.
palette_rules.photography: Bottle photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or recoloured toward the palette: no bottle, label or wine is pushed toward Claret, Vine, Brass Key or Chalk White. Correcting a frame's white balance is allowed; restyling it is not.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Reconcile records before merge and prove page, row, name, and amount completeness from the delivered artifacts.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.

values.Buyer Note: Unoaked chardonnay from Kimmeridgian marl, lean and oyster-shell mineral. Chill it well and drink it with anything from the sea.

values.Buyer Note: Pale dry Provence rose, red berry and citrus pith over a saline finish. Aperitif rose for the last of the warm evenings.

values.Buyer Note: Coastal Italian white, green almond, lemon and a faintly bitter herbal edge that loves salt and olive oil. Easy, savoury, under the radar.

values.Buyer Note: Featherweight Mosel kabinett with a touch of sweetness held up by racing acidity. Low in alcohol, high in charm, brilliant with spice.

values.Buyer Note: Austrian gruner, white pepper and green apple with a crisp savoury bite. The wine for tricky vegetables and anything from the garden.

values.Buyer Note: The co-op red, and the wine I put in more hands than any other on the shelf. Carignan and grenache off old bush vines, unoaked, bottled young and honest. Fourteen pounds, and it drinks well above that so long as you open it a good hour before dinner.

values.Wine: Domaine des Escaliers Cote Brune Syrah
values.Buyer Note: A single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah off the steep brown schist above the river, co-fermented with a little viognier the way the hill has always done it. Black olive, cracked pepper, cured meat and violets, over a tannin still coiled tight. This wants five years in the cellar, or a decanter and a long lunch if you cannot wait that long.

raw_values.Wine: Domaine des Escaliers Cote Brune Syrah
raw_values.Buyer Note: A single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah off the steep brown schist above the river, co-fermented with a little viognier the way the hill has always done it. Black olive, cracked pepper, cured meat and violets, over a tannin still coiled tight. This wants five years in the cellar, or a decanter and a long lunch if you cannot wait that long.

values.Buyer Note: A mature Piedmontese nebbiolo from a great vintage, ten years on and only now unwinding. Tar, dried rose, sour cherry and a dusting of woodsmoke over that famous grip of tannin and acid. Do not chill it and do not rush it: open it an hour ahead, pour it beside something with fat and salt, and let the middle of the bottle show you why we bought the allocation.

values.Buyer Note: Light-framed village Burgundy, red cherry and forest floor over silky tannin. Serve it cool. The gateway to proper Pinot.

values.Buyer Note: Southern Rhone grenache and syrah, warm and generous: kirsch, thyme and cocoa with a peppery lift. A fireside red at a fair price.

values.Buyer Note: The wine that changes how people think about Beaujolais. Cru gamay off granite, whole-bunch and unfiltered, so there is a savoury reduction on first pour that blows off into black cherry, iron and crushed violets. Serve it with a light chill against charcuterie or a roast chicken. If you still think gamay is thin and sweet, this is the bottle I would hand you to argue with.
